answer: Karst-cave proof: each identity surveys one limestone cave and publishes an atlas of its passages, anchored to the shale strata the public geological survey already mapped. A verifier picks a random chamber and demands a fresh depth reading within 90 seconds; a copied atlas fails because karst passages branch uniquely and shale layers bend every echo differently. One fake costs a full survey crew and a week underground; 1,000 fakes need 1,000 crews and 1,000 weeks. The atlas is the identity, and the cave cannot be photocopied.
